Class AizawaModel

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.mdi3D.view3D.aizawaDemo.AizawaModel
public class AizawaModel extends Object
Numerical model for the five-parameter Aizawa attractor.

This class owns the complete evolving state of the attractor and performs numerical integration using Apache Commons Math.

Design notes

  • This class contains no UI code.
  • The simulation thread is expected to call update().
  • The EDT is expected to call getSnapshot().
  • For simplicity, snapshot publication uses a copied packed coordinate array.

Trajectory storage

The trajectory is stored internally in a packed float array: 

[x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2, ..., xn, yn, zn]

If a maximum point count is enforced and the trajectory exceeds that size, the oldest point is discarded by shifting the packed array left by one point. This is simple and adequate for demo-scale simulations.

  • Constructor Details

    • AizawaModel

      public AizawaModel()
      Construct a model using default equations, step size, and history length.

    • AizawaModel

      public AizawaModel(AizawaEquations equations, double[] initialState, double dt, int substepsPerUpdate, int maxTrailPoints, int initialCapacity)
      Construct a model with the supplied configuration.
      Parameters:
      equations - the Aizawa equations object; must not be null
      initialState - initial state as [x, y, z]; must contain at least three values
      dt - RK4 step size; values less than or equal to zero are replaced by DEFAULT_DT
      substepsPerUpdate - number of RK4 substeps per update; values less than 1 are promoted to 1
      maxTrailPoints - maximum retained history length in points; values less than or equal to zero mean unbounded
      initialCapacity - initial internal buffer capacity in points; values less than 2 are promoted to 2

    • update

      public void update()
      Advance the model by one simulation update.

      Each call performs substepsPerUpdate RK4 substeps of size dt. After each substep, the new point is appended to the trajectory.
